findings.issue_text: [High/bug] src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py:65 — Task calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source)`, but the abstract method `sync_assignee_outbound` in `IssueSyncIntegration` (mixins/issues.py ~line 395) was not updated to accept `assignment_source`; concrete integrations overriding it with an explicit signature and no `**kwargs` will raise `TypeError` at runtime

[Medium/bug] src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:14 — `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once at import/class-definition time, so every `AssignmentSource` without an explicit `queued` shares the same timestamp; should use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`

[Medium/bug] src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py:137 — `assignment_source.to_dict()` contains a `datetime` object passed directly into Celery `apply_async(kwargs=...)`, which fails to serialize with the default JSON serializer (or round-trips as a string, leaving `queued` untyped); serialize to ISO string and parse back in `from_dict`

[Medium/bug] src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:29-34 — `from_dict` silently returns `None` on `ValueError`/`TypeError`, so a malformed `assignment_source_dict` degrades to "no source," re-enabling the outbound sync it exists to prevent (potential sync loop); a malformed source should cause the sync to be skipped instead

[Medium/test_gap] src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:411 — `sync_status_outbound` now accepts `assignment_source`, but no caller passes it and `should_sync` is never invoked with a `sync_source` for status syncs; no test or implementation for status-sync cycle prevention despite the API suggesting it

[Medium/bug] src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:13 — The `queued` field is dead code: never read anywhere in the diff (not used in `should_sync` or loop detection); remove it or wire it into cycle protection

[Low/bug] src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py:53-55 — `assignment_source` passed to integrations whose `should_sync` returns False is never used for analytics/logging; if a source is dropped there is no observability — consider logging when `assignment_source_dict` is present but unparseable

[Low/test_gap] tests/sentry/integrations/services/test_assignment_source.py:8 — `test_from_dict_empty_array` passes an empty dict, not an array, exercising the missing-required-args path instead of the empty-collection path; also missing a round-trip `to_dict()` → `from_dict()` test that would surface the datetime serialization issue

[Low/bug] src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:382-389 — Cycle check compares `sync_source.integration_id` to `self.org_integration.integration_id`, blocking A→A loops but leaving cross-integration cycles (A assigns → triggers B → B assigns back to A) possible and unhandled; no guard (hop counter or unused `queued` timestamp) limits propagation depth — document or address explicitly

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:29-34 — `from_dict` silently returns `None` on `ValueError`/`TypeError`, so a malformed `assignment_source_dict` degrades to "no source," re-enabling the outbound sync it exists to prevent (potential sync loop); a malformed source should cause the sync to be skipped instead

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `AssignmentSource.from_dict` catches `ValueError`/`TypeError` and returns `None` (new file `assignment_source.py`), and `sync_assignee_outbound` then passes `None` into `installation.should_sync(...)` (tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py). In `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync`, the cycle-prevention guard only triggers when `sync_source` is non-`None`, so a malformed `assignment_source_dict` would bypass the new guard and allow outbound sync. However, the diff doesn’t establish that malformed dicts can occur in normal operation (they’re produced via `to_dict()` in `sync_group_assignee_outbound`), so this is an input-robustness/design concern rather than a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:411 — `sync_status_outbound` now accepts `assignment_source`, but no caller passes it and `should_sync` is never invoked with a `sync_source` for status syncs; no test or implementation for status-sync cycle prevention despite the API suggesting it

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds cycle-prevention support via `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(..., sync_source)` and an `assignment_source` parameter on the abstract `sync_status_outbound(...)`, but the only concrete plumbing added is for *assignee* outbound sync: `sync_assignee_outbound` parses `assignment_source_dict` and calls `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)`. There are no corresponding changes in this diff for status outbound/inbound tasks/utilities to pass an `AssignmentSource` or to invoke `should_sync` with a source for status syncing. This makes the new status API parameter effectively unused here and leaves status sync without the same cycle-prevention/test coverage suggested by the API.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:13 — The `queued` field is dead code: never read anywhere in the diff (not used in `should_sync` or loop detection); remove it or wire it into cycle protection

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `AssignmentSource.queued` is introduced with a default (`timezone.now()`) and is only propagated via `to_dict()` (and asserted in `test_to_dict`), but it is not consulted anywhere in the newly added cycle-prevention logic (`IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync` only checks `sync_source.integration_id`). This makes the field currently unused for behavior (though not strictly “dead” since it is serialized), so the review note is a reasonable non-bug scope/cleanup concern rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py:53-55 — `assignment_source` passed to integrations whose `should_sync` returns False is never used for analytics/logging; if a source is dropped there is no observability — consider logging when `assignment_source_dict` is present but unparseable

adjudication.rationale: In `sync_assignee_outbound`, `assignment_source_dict` is parsed via `AssignmentSource.from_dict(...)`, which returns `None` on `ValueError`/`TypeError` (new file `assignment_source.py`). The task then proceeds with `parsed_assignment_source=None` and does not log/record anything about the parsing failure, and analytics are only recorded inside the `if installation.should_sync(...)` block. This is a concrete observability gap introduced by the new parsing + silent-failure behavior, but it’s not a direct correctness break shown in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a cycle-prevention check in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync` that only suppresses outbound sync when `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id` (issues.py). This explicitly still allows propagation to other linked integrations (“should still allow other integrations…” comment), so the finding’s point that cross-integration ping-pong cycles aren’t prevented (no hop counter/TTL despite `AssignmentSource.queued`) is a real, diff-grounded architectural/edge-case concern rather than a verifiable correctness bug from the shown code alone.
